failure_summary.description: The agents answered with a truth judgment, modifier, or associated medium instead of the clue's requested referent or category.
The answer was a near-match but its span or specificity differed from the requested slot, such as expanding a nickname or altering a publication or category label.
Conflicting or underspecified clues led agents to infer a plausible role rather than identify the value supported by the relevant contextual relation.

patch.reasoning: The current skill already says to identify the requested semantic type, but several answers still drifted to a related phrase or failed to match the requested answer span. A narrow rule on span and specificity makes that guidance more operational without repeating broad clue-resolution advice.

edits.content:
## Match the Answer Span to the Slot
After resolving a clue, return the value that fills the requested relation—not a neighboring full entity label or modifier. For a moniker, give the nickname itself; for the name of a publication or work, retain its attested title; for a generic category, do not add an unrequested subtype. In demonstrative fragments such as “this book,” “this type,” or “these,” resolve the demonstrative to its referent or category rather than answering with a modifier or associated medium.
